prompt_md: You start with 1 dollar against a bank with endless money. Each 1-dollar bet wins with chance 60%, and you keep betting unless you're broke. Chance you ever go broke?
prompt_short: 1 dollar, 60% bets, play forever. Chance of going broke?
hint_md: Let q be the chance of ever dropping one dollar below where you are now.
explain_intuition_md: Losing the very first bet, a 40% chance, looks like the main danger. But even after a win you can slide back, and early on you're never more than a few bad bets from zero. The chance of ever losing one dollar overall turns out to be 2 in 3.
explain_math_md: Going broke from 2 dollars means losing a net dollar twice: $$q = 0.4 + 0.6\,q^2 \;\Rightarrow\; q = \tfrac23$$ (the root below 1).
